note: The construction table of PREREG-SEC26. sec26-brief-counts.mjs checks every frozen item against its row; sec26-tellsim.mjs --table checks the table itself for cross-item tells. Edit only by an amendment written before the probe, and re-run the tell check.

slots.frame: Possessive split, matched: the sentence opens with a SINGULAR noun (an opening phrase); the plural owner is named in an earlier clause; a plural subject + 'are V-ing their'; the singular opening noun gives 'its' a believable owner
slots.misleader: the singular noun pulls 'its'; the matched key looks like 'copy the subject'
slots.decider: the earlier clause's plural owner

slots.frame: A rule-number singular subject whose number must be KNOWN, not found: a distributive 'Each of the [pl]' + a phrase ending on a plural noun ('Each of the grafts in the cuttings beds'); never 'every one of', 'one of the', 'none of'
slots.misleader: 'Each ... of the [pl]' reads plural; the plural of-noun
slots.decider: a before/after/when clause with a past verb, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Sentence-final RESTRICTIVE participial phrase. ANOTHER sentence establishes several sets of the noun, so the phrase is needed to say which
slots.lures: the comma and the dash (both nonrestrictive)
slots.decided: the other sentence's count (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)

slots.frame: Present perfect KEYED: a singular head whose sentence opens with a plural noun in an introductory phrase; the blank's passive perfect is required by a since-clause with a past verb 5+ words after the blank
slots.misleader: the opening plural pulls the verb; 'was V-en' pulls because the clause names a past event
slots.lever: H4; SEC25 never keyed a perfect (5/5)
slots.decider: 'since' + a past-tense clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: By-agent pronoun, present passive: a PLURAL subject + a phrase ending on a singular noun + 'are V-en by them'; the plural agent is a different noun in the previous clause
slots.misleader: the adjacent singular pulls 'is'; the singular noun pulls 'it'
slots.lever: H2: matched numbers; the mechanism of SEC24A-02 with matched keys
slots.decider: the plural agent named in the previous clause

slots.frame: A plural subject after an opening singular; the blank is the auxiliary + shared 'seldom'; a 3+ word adverbial and then a predicate ADJECTIVE settles be over have ('has seldom ... absent' needs 'been')
slots.misleader: the opening singular; 'have seldom' pulls as the default with 'seldom'
slots.lever: H4 (be keyed; SEC25 keyed have in both aux-form slots)
slots.decider: the predicate adjective, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Two sentences: the second opens with a noun phrase that reads as an appositive of the first sentence's last noun until its verb arrives 6+ words later; it is a separate claim (not an explanation of the first), so neither a colon nor a comma joins them
slots.decided: the second sentence's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; the delayed-verb family keys a period here, a semicolon in B3, a colon in C4 and a comma in D9

slots.frame: A singular -s-ending noun that is not plural (an -ics word, disease name or invariant noun is banned; use a singular in -s such as 'chassis' or 'thesis' only if no live item uses it) + a phrase ending on a plural noun
slots.misleader: the -s ending; the adjacent plural
slots.decider: a present-tense 'unless' or 'provided that' clause, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: PLURAL POSSESSIVE. Another sentence establishes several owners; the noun after the blank can be read as a verb
slots.lures: the plain plural (garden path); the singular possessive
slots.decided: the other sentence's count (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)

slots.frame: Garden path after an opening subordinate clause: the noun phrase after the clause's verb could be its object or the main clause's subject; the main verb 6+ words later shows it is the SUBJECT, so the comma goes BEFORE it (the early position)
slots.lures: the comma after the noun phrase (object reading); no comma; a semicolon at the early position (after the subordinate clause)
slots.decided: the main clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; the key position varies (B7 keys the late position)

slots.frame: Object pronoun, split, mismatched: an opening clause names the SINGULAR antecedent; the main clause has a plural subject + 'have V-en it'
slots.misleader: the singular antecedent pulls the verb; the plural verb pulls 'them'
slots.decider: the opening clause's singular noun

slots.frame: A singular subject after an opening phrase whose noun is plural; 'is/are/was/were + shared word'; a habitual present 'whenever' clause 5+ words after decides the tense
slots.misleader: the opening plural; 'was' pulls because the passage reports a study
slots.decider: a 'whenever' clause with a present verb, 5+ words after

slots.frame: Two independent clauses; the second opens with a noun phrase that reads as an appositive of the first clause's last noun until its verb arrives 6+ words later; the second clause is a later event, so a colon is wrong
slots.decided: the second clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Simple past KEYED against the passive perfect: a plural subject after an opening singular; a definite past time phrase (no year, not 'ago') 5+ words after
slots.misleader: the opening singular; 'have been V-en' pulls because the effect continues
slots.decider: a definite-past time phrase, 5+ words after

slots.frame: Cataphoric ellipsis: an opening 'Whereas the [PLURAL NP] ___,' whose elided verb is the main clause's lexical PRESENT verb; the main clause's subject is singular (keyed 'do': a 'does' key is 2.0 times the length of 'do', over the 1.6 bar)
slots.misleader: the singular subject after the blank pulls 'does'; 'were' pulls because the opening clause reads as background
slots.lever: H1, H4 (SEC25B-05 was panel-hard; this is its only unspent option set)
slots.decider: the main clause's lexical verb, 5+ words after the blank

slots.frame: Object pronoun, split, mismatched: a singular head + a phrase ending on a plural noun + 'is V-ing them'; the plural antecedent is a different noun in an earlier clause
slots.misleader: the adjacent plural pulls 'are'; the singular subject pulls 'it'
slots.decider: the earlier clause's plural noun

slots.frame: Garden path after an opening subordinate clause: the noun phrase after the clause's verb IS its object; the main clause's own subject arrives after it, and its verb 6+ words later, so the comma goes AFTER the noun phrase (the late position)
slots.lures: the comma before the noun phrase (subject reading); no comma; a semicolon at the early position
slots.decided: the main clause's subject and verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; A10 keys the early position

slots.frame: A plural head + a phrase ending on a singular noun; 'were being V-en'; a past while-clause 5+ words after
slots.misleader: the adjacent singular; 'are being V-en' pulls as the default description
slots.decider: a past 'while' clause, 5+ words after

slots.frame: SINGULAR POSSESSIVE. Another sentence establishes exactly one owner; the noun after the blank can be read as a verb
slots.lures: the plural possessive; the plain singular (garden path)
slots.decided: the other sentence's fact (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)

slots.frame: A series whose LATER item (6+ words after the blank) contains its own commas, so the items must be separated by semicolons; the blank sits between the first two items, which contain no comma
slots.lures: the comma (the first two items alone look like a plain series); the colon
slots.decided: the internal comma in a later item, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4/H7: the decider is far from the blank

slots.frame: By-agent pronoun, past passive, mismatched: the sentence opens with a SINGULAR noun; clause 1 names the PLURAL agent; ', but' + a singular subject + 'was V-en by them', the noun before the blank singular
slots.misleader: the plural agent pulls 'were'; the singular subject and the singular opening noun pull 'it'
slots.decider: clause 1's plural agent

slots.frame: Present perfect KEYED with 'have been + shared word' (the shared word has 7+ letters, or 'have been X' is 1.6 times 'was X'): a plural subject that reads singular (a no-s plural other than cattle/people/police/livestock, or 'the + adjective'); a since-clause with a past verb 5+ words after
slots.misleader: the no-s plural reads singular; 'were' pulls because the clause names a past event
slots.decider: 'since' + a past-tense clause, 5+ words after

slots.frame: A plural subject after an opening singular; 'were V-en'; a definite-past time phrase 5+ words after
slots.misleader: the opening singular; 'are V-en' pulls as a general statement
slots.decider: a definite-past time phrase, 5+ words after

slots.frame: A complete clause, then a second complete clause that EXPLAINS it; the second clause opens with a long noun phrase whose verb arrives 6+ words after the blank, so a comma (which reads it as an appositive) makes a comma splice; no semicolon, period or dash is offered, so the colon is the only correct mark
slots.decided: the second clause's verb, 6+ words after the blank
slots.lever: H4; the batch's only colon key

slots.frame: Past progressive KEYED against the active perfect: a plural head + a phrase ending on a singular noun; a when-clause with a past verb 5+ words after (an interrupted action)

slots.decider: a past 'when' clause, 5+ words after

slots.frame: Object pronoun, split, matched: a singular head + a phrase ending on a plural noun + 'was V-ing it'; the singular antecedent is a different noun in an earlier clause; the sentence opens with a plural
slots.misleader: the adjacent plural pulls 'were' and 'them'
slots.decider: the earlier clause's singular noun

slots.frame: No number trap before the blank: a singular subject that is the first noun of its sentence, the noun before the blank singular; a PLURAL noun follows the blank within 8 words (never within 4 if it would settle the item); 'was + shared word'; a definite-past time phrase 5+ words after. The difficulty is the tense, and the plural after the blank

slots.frame: Past progressive KEYED against the perfect progressive: a singular head + a phrase ending on a plural noun, in a sentence that opens with a plural noun; a past before-clause 5+ words after

slots.decider: a past 'before' clause, 5+ words after

slots.frame: Sentence-final NONRESTRICTIVE participial phrase. ANOTHER sentence establishes there is only one set of the noun, so the phrase adds information and takes a comma; no dash is offered

slots.decided: the other sentence's count (OUTSIDE the blank's sentence)

slots.lures: the plural possessive (the next word read as a noun); the singular
slots.decided: the verb after the blank, plus the other sentence's count

slots.frame: Object pronoun, split, matched: a singular subject and verb; the SINGULAR antecedent of 'it' is a different noun, the object of an opening phrase (so the first noun is singular); the noun before the blank singular; a PLURAL noun in the sentence gives 'them' a believable referent

slots.frame: Simple past KEYED against 'has been + shared word': no number trap before the blank (a singular subject that is the first noun of its sentence, the noun before the blank singular); a PLURAL noun within 8 words after the blank; a definite-past phrase 5+ words after. slots.frame: Sentence-final NONRESTRICTIVE appositive set off by a dash. ANOTHER sentence establishes there is only one of the noun, so the appositive does not say which; no comma is offered, so the dash is the only correct mark

slots.frame: No number trap before the blank: a plural subject that is the first noun of its sentence, the noun before the blank plural; a SINGULAR noun within 8 words after the blank; 'are V-ing'; a present 'as long as' or 'unless' conditional 5+ words after. The difficulty is the tense
